doc.title: Mose Allison — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: I'm Not Talking, Numbers on Paper and other favorites
summary: Amy picks favorites and recites I'm Not Talking.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: So we have a wide pool of sources from which you’re refracting your lyrics and stories. To me, it seems almost... Please forgive me for making these leaps, I don’t know you at all, but when you were discussing the short stories, a lot of these lyrics sound like they could be a
short story in... Each of these songs contains a complete world. Amy, does anything else leap out at you from that list?

“I’m not Talking.” That’s one that the Yardbirds did. That was “Don’t ask me what I have to say / If I said things were splendid / Someone would be offended / If I said things were awful / It might just be unlawful / I’m not talking of just okay.” That’s one that is on The Word From Mose. I always liked “You Can Count On Me To Do My Part.” I like that one, because that’s about...
And how about “Numbers On Paper”? But that came later.
Oh, that’s much later, but that’s a beautiful song, “Numbers On Paper.”
I know some...did some mathematician in a Ph.D paper quote “Numbers On Paper”?
I don’t know. But that’s the one that Frank Black from the Pixies sang on in the documentary.
